title: On AI and Knowledge — Pablo Castro, Distinguished Engineer & CVP for AI Knowledge, Microsoft
talk_summary: Pablo Castro frames agent knowledge as intrinsic (model weights), extrinsic (retrieval/grounding), and learned (process improvement loops), and demos Microsoft Foundry IQ knowledge bases plus an 'agent optimizer' that hill-climbs agent configuration against an eval. The only directly copyable mechanism is the externalized-config + eval-driven optimization loop; the rest is product framing.

takeaways.what_they_do: Require agent instructions, tool definitions, and skills to be externalized config; generate a task-adherence eval dataset from traces/instructions, then run an optimizer that iterates candidate configs (GEPA-style loop) against the rubric and applies the best one.
takeaways.numbers: optimize run ~45 minutes; baseline vs optimized config compared on eval

takeaways.what_they_do: If no eval exists, derive a task-adherence eval dataset automatically from existing agent traces and instructions rather than hand-writing test cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you don't, you can actually say eval generate and what we'll do is we'll look at what we know about the agent like traces and instructions

takeaways.technique: Hybrid retrieval beats single-method; agentic retrieval for hard cases
takeaways.what_they_do: Combine lexical + vector + other retrieval methods rather than relying on cosine similarity alone, and add an agentic retrieval layer that reflects on whether the information need was satisfied before returning.
takeaways.numbers: claims better evidence recall and answer completeness for agentic retrieval, no hard numbers given

takeaways.technique: Token-efficiency as an explicit retrieval design goal
takeaways.what_they_do: Evaluate retrieval systems on information density — fewest tokens for the most useful answer — not just relevance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we carefully evaluate this system to make sure that we give you the most information dense answer that has the fewest tokens

takeaways.technique: Knowledge base exposed as MCP server
takeaways.what_they_do: Every knowledge base is a standalone MCP server, so any harness can connect without glue code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every knowledge base is an MCP server, so you can just connect to it uh without having to write any glue code
